deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 6-9). Grothendieck axiomatizes a 'modèle' M_* = (M_n)_n, where each M_n is a family of 'tame' (modérées) subsets of R^n. In modern terms this is essentially a first-order structure, or o-minimal-type structure, on a set R, given by its definable sets. From it he builds the category Σ = E = Esp_mod (= Esp_{M_*}) of tame spaces. Morphisms are tame maps, i.e. maps whose graph is tame. Page 7 showed that giving M_* is equivalent to giving a triple (E, R, |.|): E has finite limits, |.| : E -> Ens is left exact, and every object embeds in some R^n. Section (III) of the plan, begun on page 7, concerns colimits ('limites inductives', 'jonctions') in Esp_mod.

This page:

(1) A heavily reworked Proposition on the existence of finite sums in Σ. The struck attempts read 'R_0 ≠ ∅' and 'Hom_Σ(R^0, R) ≠ ∅' with R^0 = {e}. The final hypothesis is written above: 'card R_0 ≥ 2'. Here R_0 is apparently the set of tame (0-definable) points of R, i.e. Hom_Σ({e}, R). The conclusion, completed by the axiom (M5) stated on the next page (each M_n is stable under finite unions, ∅ ∈ M_n), is that Σ has finite sums and X -> |X| commutes with them. The intended proof is the standard one: pick two tame points a ≠ b in R and realise X_1 ⊔ X_2 inside R^{n+1} as (X_1 × {a}) ∪ (X_2 × {b}).

(2) A Corollary. On a finite sum (disjoint union) there is one and only one tame structure for which the pieces of the 'discrete stratification' are tame. The marginal note says this should instead be deduced as a corollary of the next proposition.

(3) An announced construction: the amalgamated sum X_1 ⊔_Z X_2 without a hypothesis on Z (word unclear). This is taken up on the next page as a 'Question'.

(4) Proposition. Let I be a finite diagram type and (X_i) an I-diagram of tame spaces. Let X be the colimit in Ens, a quotient of the set ⊔X_i. If X admits a tame structure making all canonical maps g_i : X_i -> X tame, then X with this structure is a colimit of the X_i in Σ.

Proof sketch (not written on the page). Take a cocone f_i : X_i -> Y, and let f : X -> Y be the induced map of sets. Since ⊔X_i -> X is surjective, graph(f) = ∪_i (g_i, f_i)(X_i). Each term is the image of a tame set under a tame map, hence tame by stability under projections. The union is finite, hence tame by (M5). So f is tame. Such a structure is also unique: two of them would both be colimits, and the identity map would be tame in both directions.

Purpose: build gluings (definable spaces) and finite colimits in the category of tame spaces, as part of the foundations of 'topologie modérée'.
errors: The final Proposition tacitly uses that images of tame sets under tame maps are tame (projection axiom) and finite unions (M5). (M5) is only formally introduced on the next page, so the page is logically out of order; Grothendieck's margin note acknowledges the reordering.

The finite-sums Proposition is left in a messy state: several hypotheses are struck out ('R_0 ≠ ∅', 'Hom(R^0,R) ≠ ∅'). The correct hypothesis, at least two distinct tame points, is added above the line. Without two definable constants finite coproducts need not exist, so the correction is mathematically right.

ideas.what: Finite coproducts of tame spaces exist when R has at least two tame (0-definable) points, using M5, and the forgetful functor preserves them.
ideas.modern_name: Existence of disjoint unions in the category of definable sets given two distinct definable constants
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of model theory / categorical logic (definable sets with two constants form an extensive category; cf. Makkai–Reyes 1977, M^eq constructions)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, without these details

ideas.what: A set-theoretic colimit of a finite diagram of tame spaces, if it carries a tame structure making the canonical maps tame, is the categorical colimit.
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / quotients of definable spaces; the forgetful functor creates finite colimits under a definability hypothesis
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Tame Topology and O-minimal Structures (1998), ch. 10 (definable spaces, definable quotients)
ideas.where_published: unpublished; general program in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Unique tame structure on a finite disjoint union making the pieces (discrete stratification) tame.
ideas.modern_name: Definable disjoint union / definable space with a finite atlas

deep.surprise_reason: Careful foundational bookkeeping for an axiomatic tame-topology category: finite coproducts given two definable constants, and colimits created by the forgetful functor. It is correct but standard, and later appears in o-minimal and categorical-logic literature. Its interest is historical: an early (1970s) unpublished categorical treatment of o-minimal-type structures, already documented as part of Grothendieck's tame topology project.
transcription_corrections: 'quotient d'un certain quotient de ⊔X_i (ensemble commun [?])' probably reads '(ensemble somme)', i.e. a quotient of the set-theoretic sum ⊔X_i.
'Supposons qu'il existe une X une structure modérée' should read 'Supposons qu'il existe sur X une structure modérée'.
'Corollaire Sur toute union finie [?] dans Σ' more likely reads 'Sur toute somme finie dans Σ'.
The struck 'Hom_Σ(R^0, R) ≠ ∅' has 'R^0 = {e}' written beneath it (the Σ = {e} line is that annotation).
'sans supposer Z [?]': the word after Z is unclear, perhaps 'lisse' or 'fermé'; uncertain.
Final line: 'est une limite inductive des X_i'.
